title: Field Notes Crossword -  A puzzle game that uses the Prompt API for infinite crosswords
author: theoakbear
selftext:
Field Notes is a crossword puzzle game that builds puzzles via the [Prompt API](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/prompt-api). It starts by selecting a theme, then creating words and finally creating clues for those words all in the browser. A local packer then builds a grid in a way that tries to maximize intersections.

I started this demo out of curiosity, mainly to see how Prompt API models can be integrated in games. My experience so far has been that it's fast enough to live in level generation but models not really there yet when it comes to complex instructions like generating a full grid for a level and associated descriptions. 

If you prompt them to “make a 9×9 crossword,” you get:

* words that don’t share letters where they should
* lengths that don’t match the slots
* clues like "concept related to trees"

I tried to solve this problem by prompting initially, but always got some variation of those issues. So I went for an algorithmic solution instead where I could generate words and solutions individually.

The loop

1. Pick a theme from a fixed list.
2. Ask Prompt API for *more words than the grid needs*, with a mix of lengths the packer actually wants (`3–5` on a mini, longer on 9×9 / 13×13).
3. Throw away anything that isn’t `A–Z`, the right length, unique, or a real clue. Vague “related to / associated with / a concept” phrases are filtered at this stage.
4. Run a greedy packer: seed two words that cross, then keep placing entries that *must* cross existing letters. Change background on whatever is left empty.
5. If there aren't enough words, ask the model for another batch on the same theme (“already have: OAK, RAIN, …”) and try again. Three attempts total, if there aren't enough words by the end then fail the level generation. Hasn't happened so far on 10+ games.

A 5×5 only needs about ten clues so the algorithm asks for 22 entries to make this work. It makes the generation unique enough while also being deterministic so you can generate crosswords that are solvable.

Made it open source and available on Github Pages: [https://steven-moss-notebook.github.io/FieldNoteCrossword/](https://steven-moss-notebook.github.io/FieldNoteCrossword/)

Hope you enjoy it! Feedback would be highly appreciated!
